reason: Letters are spelled as themselves.
Digits, ., _, ~ and - are spelled as themselves.
A + is outside the set and is percent-encoded, as a package directory may hold it.
A space is percent-encoded.
A % is itself percent-encoded.
A # is percent-encoded.
A non-ASCII byte is outside the Go set and is percent-encoded byte by byte, with uppercase digits.
A byte that opens no well-formed UTF-8 sequence is percent-encoded.
The lowest control byte is percent-encoded.
A control byte is percent-encoded.
A space is percent-encoded.
DEL is percent-encoded.
The first byte past the space is spelled as itself.
A space inside a file name is percent-encoded and the rest is spelled as itself.
A # is percent-encoded, so the first # still splits the scope from the fragment.
A % is itself percent-encoded.
A * is percent-encoded, so a path never holds a pattern's wildcard.
A ? is percent-encoded, so a path never holds a pattern's wildcard.
Quote, brackets, backslash, colon, ~ and + are spelled as themselves in a source path.
Well-formed two-, three- and four-byte UTF-8 sequences are spelled as themselves.
A lone continuation byte is percent-encoded.
A byte that is never part of UTF-8 is percent-encoded.
A truncated three-byte sequence is percent-encoded byte by byte.
An overlong encoding is not well formed and is percent-encoded byte by byte.
The bytes of a lone UTF-16 surrogate are not well-formed UTF-8 and are percent-encoded byte by byte.
A file operand percent-encodes the quote, the brackets, the backslash and the colon, which sit in the fragment, and the space.
A file operand percent-encodes #, %, * and ? as a source path does.
Non-ASCII, !, ~ and + are spelled as themselves in a file operand.
NEL, U+0085, is a C1 control and whitespace, and is percent-encoded byte by byte.
The first and last C1 controls, U+0080 and U+009F, are percent-encoded.
A no-break space, U+00A0, is whitespace and is percent-encoded.
U+00A1, the first code point past the no-break space, is spelled as itself.
The Ogham space mark and the first and last of the spaces U+2000 to U+200A are percent-encoded.
U+200B, U+2027 and U+2030, beside the whitespace, are no whitespace and are spelled as themselves.
The line and paragraph separators are whitespace and are percent-encoded.
U+202F, U+205F, the ideographic space and U+FEFF are whitespace and are percent-encoded.
A file operand percent-encodes the whitespace past ASCII as a source path does.
Three dots are a file name, spelled as themselves.
Dots before another byte are spelled as themselves.
An escape of a byte the set spells as itself is not canonical.
A raw byte outside the set is not a spelling.
Escape digits are uppercase hexadecimal.
An escape of the separator decodes to a byte no segment holds.
Escape digits are uppercase hexadecimal.
A % that opens no escape is not a spelling.
A % followed by one digit opens no escape.
A % followed by a letter past F opens no escape.
A well-formed non-ASCII sequence is spelled as itself in a source path, not escaped.
A raw space is not a spelling.
A segment is never empty.
An escape of a byte the set spells as itself is not canonical.
A raw quote is not a spelling of a file operand.
A raw colon is not a spelling of a file operand.
A raw C1 control is not a spelling.
A raw no-break space is not a spelling.
A raw line separator is not a spelling.
A raw ideographic space is not a spelling of a file operand.
A segment that decodes to . names no file a reference scopes.
A segment that decodes to .. names no file a reference scopes and leads a reader out of its directory.
A segment that decodes to .. is not an import path element.
A segment that decodes to . is not a file operand segment.
A Bidi_Control character, here the right-to-left override, is in the unsafe set and is percent-encoded byte by byte.
The Arabic letter mark, U+061C, is a Bidi_Control character and is percent-encoded.
The left-to-right isolate, U+2066, is percent-encoded in a file operand too.
A raw Bidi_Control character is not a spelling.
A raw pop of an isolate is not a spelling.
The zero-width joiner, U+200D, is no Bidi_Control character and stands as itself.
